[Startup Exploration: Part 3] Electricity is no longer enough. Semiconductors connected by light, the current state of silicon photonics

As the computational load of AI increases, semiconductors struggle before they can get faster. They generate heat. They consume power. It becomes difficult to carry signals over long distances. The very premise of connecting with electricity is beginning to show its limits little by little. This has led to the emergence of the idea of carrying signals with light. It sounds like a future technology
Introduction: An era where "how to connect" is more important than computation
Increasing GPUs → Data movement volume surges → Wiring power and heat increase → Connection becomes more difficult than the computing unit

The competition for AI semiconductors is no longer decided solely by "how fast they can calculate." This is because how you connect a large number of GPUs and accelerators determines both performance and power consumption. In fact, NVIDIA itself has launched switch products using silicon photonics, and light is no longer a laboratory topic; it has entered the design theory of AI infrastructure.

What is important here is that this is not about light "completely driving out electricity." At least for the time being, copper wiring will remain for short distances and some connections. In fact, Jensen Huang also indicated at GTC in March 2026 that he intends to use both copper and light in the next generation. In other words, the battle is not about making everything light, but about where it
